FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to enable non-interactive package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Update package lists and install all necessary dependencies in a single layer.
# This includes:
# - build-essential, g++, cmake: Core C++ build toolchain.
# - git: For cloning the application source code.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries for MPI support.
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communications (e.g., git clone over https).
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    cmake \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    ca-certificates \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for container compatibility.
# This is required to allow MPI processes to run as the root user inside a container.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Set a build directory
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the Kripke source code from the official LLNL repository.
# FIX: The repository's primary branch is 'master', not 'main'. This corrects the git clone failure.
# The '--recurse-submodules' flag is required to fetch the BLT build system dependency.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --recurse-submodules -b master https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git .

# Configure the Kripke build using CMake in an out-of-source build directory.
# - DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Creates a performance-optimized executable.
# - DENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support as required.
RUN cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DENABLE_MPI=ON

# Compile the application using all available CPU cores to speed up the build process.
RUN cmake --build build --parallel $(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a standard system path.
# This ensures the 'kripke' command is available globally in the container's PATH.
# The original executable is named kripke.exe by the build system.

# Clean up by removing the source and build directories to reduce the final image size.
RUN rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container's runtime.
WORKDIR /

# Define the default command. Running the application without arguments will display its usage information.
CMD ["kripke"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the Kripke proxy application
# on a single node within a Kubernetes cluster using the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A unique name for the MiniCluster resource.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # Deployment will occur in the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. For a single-node run, this is 1.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across the MiniCluster.
  # The Flux Operator will prepend 'flux run -n 1' to the command.
  tasks: 1

  # When set to false, the MiniCluster pods and services are not
  # deleted after the job completes, allowing for inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging configuration for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

  # Defines the container that will run the application workload.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to execute. The Flux Operator wraps this with 'flux run'.
      # Kripke is run with no additional parameters as requested.
      command: kripke
      # This container is a worker, not the one that launches the flux broker.
      # The Flux Operator injects a separate container for that purpose.
      launcher: false

# This MiniCluster manifest is corrected to resolve an application assertion error.
# The number of zones in the Z-dimension is adjusted to be divisible by the number of processes.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name and namespace remain unchanged.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster remains 1 for a single-node run.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks remains 48.
  tasks: 48

  # The pod is still scheduled on the c7a.12xlarge instance type.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "c7a.12xlarge"

  # Defines the container that will run the application workload.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # FIX: Adjusted the number of zones in the Z-dimension from 40 to 39.
      # This is required because the number of zones must be evenly divisible
      # by the number of processes in that dimension (39 is divisible by 3).
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,3 --zones 40,40,39
      # This container is a worker, not the launcher.
      launcher: false

  # Logging configuration remains the same.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # cleanup remains false to allow for post-run inspection.
  cleanup: false

This attempt selects a 64-core ARM HPC instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) and parallelizes the workload across all 64 cores with an increased problem size, which is expected to drastically improve performance.

The problem decomposition and workload per task have been adjusted accordingly to match the new core count and to increase computational intensity, which may yield better efficiency.

This resulted in an astronomically large total problem size that exceeded instance memory. This attempt corrects the configuration by using a much more reasonable workload per task ('--zones 12,12,12') on the 64-core ARM instance to properly test its scaling performance.

All previous parallel attempts performed significantly worse than the initial single-core baseline. This is likely due to misconfiguring the problem size, either making it too large and exhausting memory (runs 2, 3) or too small for the core count, resulting in poor scaling from communication overhead (run 4). This attempt will increase the workload per core by raising the '--zones' parameter to a moderate level on the 64-core ARM instance, aiming to find a better computation-to-communication ratio.

All previous parallel attempts on ARM and AMD architectures resulted in extremely poor performance, orders of magnitude worse than the single-core baseline. This suggests issues with either memory bandwidth, communication overhead, or an improper workload size. This attempt switches to a compute-optimized Intel instance (c6in.12xlarge) and further increases the per-task workload (--zones 24,24,24) to test a different hardware profile and attempt to find a better computation-to-communication ratio.

After multiple attempts at parallelization across different CPU architectures (ARM, AMD, Intel) and problem sizes, every multi-task configuration resulted in a Figure of Merit that was orders of magnitude worse than the initial single-task baseline (8.77e-8 vs ~1e-9). This indicates that for this workload, the MPI communication overhead on a single node outweighs any benefits of parallel execution. The single-task configuration is therefore the optimal one found. The final manifest reflects this, running a single task on a compute-optimized instance to maximize single-core performance.
